market_snapshot.notes: Tue Nov 24, 7:00 AM PT post-open (first 30 min of regular session). Cash-session figures per Investopedia live page (crawled 14:45 UTC) and Pulsafi 9:34 AM ET. Monday closes: S&P 7,237.17 (+4.73%), Nasdaq 24,089.56 (+6.51%), Dow 49,595.31 (+3.01%), VIX 26.62. Market closed Thu Nov 26 for Thanksgiving; half day Fri Nov 27. WTI ranged roughly $79.6-$81.15 across wires this morning as oil swings on Iran headlines.

headlines.headline: Major indexes slide in the first 30 minutes: Nasdaq -1.7%, S&P 500 -1.0%, Dow -0.2% in early trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: The premarket giveback is now a real session decline — Monday's historic rally is giving back about a fifth of its S&P gain in the first half hour.

headlines.headline: Nvidia -6%+ in early trading after soaring 31% Monday and adding more than $900B in market value; still down more than 30% from its Oct 6 record closing high.
headlines.why_it_matters: Profit-taking plus the unresolved governance overhang (SEC probe, Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Dec 1 House testimony) is outweighing the reinstatement rally.

headlines.headline: Chip selloff broadens: Micron and AMD -8%, Intel, Marvell and SK Hynix -5%+, Broadcom -4%; SOXX and the Roundhill Memory ETF each -6%+.
headlines.why_it_matters: Sector-wide unwind, not a single-name move — the whole AI hardware complex is retracing Monday's surge together.

headlines.headline: HPE -14% in early trading despite beating expectations and raising guidance; Dell -9% ahead of its Q3 print after the close (after +20% Monday).
headlines.why_it_matters: The beat-and-fall pattern is now the morning's dominant theme — the bar is the AI-server guide and demand durability, and Dell is the next check.

headlines.headline: Anthropic -7% in early trading, below the $83 IPO price, on pace for a third straight down session.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade's newest public name is under water vs its IPO price within a week — sentiment is cooling across the whole AI complex, not just hardware.

headlines.headline: Mega-caps mostly lower in early trading: Amazon -2%, Meta and Alphabet ~-1%, Tesla -1.7%; Apple flat, Microsoft slightly higher.
headlines.why_it_matters: The giveback is concentrated in AI-linked names while the least AI-exposed mega-caps hold up — rotation, not a broad risk-off day.

headlines.headline: Sanofi's $41B Insmed acquisition lifts Insmed +14% and Sanofi's US-traded shares +8% in early trading.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning's biggest deal is a defensive-sector counterweight to the tech selloff — M&A appetite is alive even on a down tape.

headlines.headline: Case-Shiller: US home prices +2.1% y/y in September, unchanged from August; 20-city +2.6% vs +2.7% expected; 16th straight month of real-term declines as 3.7% inflation outran the gain.
headlines.why_it_matters: In-line and lagged, so it barely moves the tape — but it keeps the housing-affordability drag in view ahead of 10 AM consumer confidence.

headlines.headline: Iran claims three tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz; Bessent widened sanctions on 2 dozen+ Iranian exchange houses and front companies; Trump said diplomacy continues but attacks could resume after the New Year.
headlines.why_it_matters: Fresh Hormuz risk on a day oil is already swinging — but Gulf exports have rebounded to 74% of prewar levels and the IEA sees a surplus, so crude is whipsawing rather than spiking. The mine claims are unverified — treat as fragile.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news; fresh Nov 24 Zacks analysis highlights the $500M order book through 2029, with >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted and revenue per horsepower +8% y/y. Carry-forward: Q3 2026 (Nov 3) — revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M, DCF $495-505M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027. WTI $81.15 (+1.2%) but swinging on Iran headlines.

watch_next: Consumer confidence at 10 AM ET (7 AM PT) — expected 92.4 vs 91.7 prior — the first demand read before Wednesday's PCE/GDP dump.
FOMC meeting minutes at 2 PM ET — the next input on the near-certain December hike (97.6% priced for 25bp).
After-close earnings: Dell, HP, Workday, Ambarella — Dell is the next check on AI server demand after HPE's guide-driven selloff.
Best Buy earnings call at 8 AM ET — color on the AI gadget upgrade cycle and holiday demand.
NVDA overhangs still live: Bessent's Nov 25 deadline, Huang's Dec 1 House testimony, the SEC probe — plus whether the chip pullback stabilizes or deepens into the close.
Thanksgiving-week tape: market closed Thu Nov 26, half day Fri Nov 27; thin liquidity can amplify moves.
analysis: What changed vs the 6 AM brief: the premarket giveback became a real early-session slide — Nasdaq -1.7% and S&P -1.0% in the first 30 minutes, roughly in line with futures, and the VIX jumped above 29 (+10.2%). HPE worsened from -12% premarket to -14% in the session, and Dell slid 9% into its after-close print. Case-Shiller landed in line (+2.1% y/y) and barely registered. One correction to carry: ADI's premarket print is conflicting across sources — one wire had it -10% on a soft guide, another -2.5% after a Q4 beat (EPS $4.06 vs $3.89 expected) — so don't anchor on the ADI number. Signal vs noise: the beat-and-fall pattern broadening across the AI complex, Anthropic under its IPO price, and the VIX spike are signal; the exact early-session percentages and the oil whipsaw on unverified Hormuz mine claims are noise. The next real tests are consumer confidence at 10 AM ET, FOMC minutes at 2 PM ET, and Dell after the close.

community_signals.title: Investigation of Polymarket Insider Trading on the Reinstatement of Jensen Huang
community_signals.takeaway: A French on-chain investigation claims a fresh wallet bet $4,648 at 6.5% odds on Huang's reinstatement 89 minutes before Trump's public post, netting ~$71,500 — adding an information-asymmetry angle to the Huang story. Commenters are split: some call the timing damning, others say $70K is small and could be luck, and note the piece itself is LLM-assisted research.
